speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant have a history of cystic fibrosis, and do you notice any "currant jelly" stools? REQUEST TEST: Sweat chloride test.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal sweat chloride test, cystic fibrosis is unlikely, pointing toward a mechanical obstruction like Hirschsprung's disease. I will perform a digital rectal examination to assess for a tight anal sphincter and check for an explosion of stool upon withdrawal.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of meconium passage and bilious vomiting strongly suggest Hirschsprung's disease. I will perform a rectal biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells. REQUEST TEST: Rectal Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rectal biopsy confirms the absence of ganglion cells, which is diagnostic for Hirschsprung's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
